# Introduction

This is a **tutorial** on using R studio to setup a generic file structure that you can share with collaborators for any coding project that you are about to undertake.

Additionally at the end I discrbe how to insert screenshots into knit files. 

## Using the **here** package

Creating reproducible code that you can share is essential in all the analysis that we do!

The **here** package can really help with this!

https://github.com/jennybc/here_here

I have found that using the here package, in parallel with a synced shared folder on OneDrive or Dropbox is the most efficient way to share and troubleshoot and share code. 

There may be other (and better) ways of doing this (perhaps pushing code to Github?), but I haven't found one yet. 

## File structure is so important!

While each project is unique, I have found there are some universal aspects to each project that can organized effecienty with a thoughtful file structure. 

What we wnat to avoid is a lot of files in one folder and not knowing where certain files are when we want to look them up or share them. 

Therefore, I suggest for every project that you start, that you maintain the file structure I'm describing in this tutorial at a minimum. Feel free to expand on it or customize it depending on the needs of the project that you are working on. 

# Step 1

Create a new folder with the name of the project that you are starting. Then copy and paste this setup file into that folder. 

![](`r here::here("Images", "Screenshot 1.png")`)

**IMPORTANT**

Now close R studio and re-open it by double clicking on the setup.RMD file that you placed in the new project folder. 

R studio will recognize this new folder as the location to place the files that will be created by the next command. 

You can double check that you hae the right folder location by checking the directory in the consol like below:

![](`r here::here("Images", "R Console.png")`)

You can also always use the "here()" command in the consol to check for your current **here location**.

# Step 2

## Create .here file to orient files to relative directory

This line of code will create an anchor location from which the **here** package will recognize as home (no matter what computer folder is synced to)

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}

here::set_here()

#Check where here directory
here()

```

After running this command you should see a .here file in the folder

![](`r here::here("Images", "Screenshot 2.png")`)

# Step 3

## Setup file architecture

In order to give the files names, we need to save those names as strings the R studio environment. 

I have found that the bare-minimum files that I like to have for every project that I start are 

**Code** : Where .RMD and knit files will live. <br>
**Dataset** : Where the original data files will live (cell ranger outputs or .rds files). <br>
**Output** : Where the objects of your analysis will live. <br>
**Images** : Where screenshots that give your analysis context will live. <br>
**Papers** : Where papers relevant to the project will life. <br>

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}

Code <- "Code"
Dataset <- "Dataset"
Output <- "Output"
Images <- "Images"
Papers <- "Papers"

```

After running this chuck you should see the values in your **Environment**.

![](`r here::here("Images", "Screenshot 3.png")`)

# Step 4

Create a folder called output in the New Project Folder

This line of code reads "If the directory called "Output" doesn't exist, then create it"

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}

if (!dir.exists(here(Output))) {dir.create(here(Output))}

```

Now you should be able to see the **Output** file in the home folder

![](`r here::here("Images", "Screenshot 4.png")`)

## Create the rest of the folders

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}

if (!dir.exists(here(Code))) {dir.create(here(Code))}
if (!dir.exists(here(Dataset))) {dir.create(here(Dataset))}
if (!dir.exists(here(Images))) {dir.create(here(Images))}
if (!dir.exists(here(Output))) {dir.create(here(Output))}
if (!dir.exists(here(Papers))) {dir.create(here(Papers))}

```

Now the rest of the files should be created into the folder. 

![](`r here::here("Images", "Screenshot 5.png")`)

## You can created **nested** files

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}

Temp <- "Temp"

if (!dir.exists(here("Output", Temp))) {dir.create(here("Output", Temp))}

```

![](`r here::here("Images", "Screenshot 6.png")`)

# Adding Screenshots

I have found that adding screenshots into knit files a powerful way for sharing my train of thought and documenting experimental outcomes. 

I have screenshoted pictures of protocols, websites, twitter, and manuscripts (just to name a few). 

The way that I organize these screenshots is using the following code:

![](`r here::here("Images", "Screenshot 7.png")`)

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# ![](`r here::here("Images", "Screenshot 6.png")`)

```

In between the brackets you can add a caption (I usually don't).

And then the **here** package looks for the screenshots in the "Images" folder (the location you can keep every screenshot that you want to render with the knit file)
